simple.meaning: אַחְלָמָה (ʼachlâmâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a gem, probably the amethyst.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַחְלָמָה (H306) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 28:19, with occurrences in Exodus.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַחְלָמָה (H306) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַחְלָמָה (H306) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַחְלָמָה (ʼachlâmâh) / H306 is traced through Exodus 28:19, Exodus 39:12 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H306. achlamah אַחְלָ֑מָה noun feminine perhaps amethyst (etymology dubious; below חלם Thes q. v.; Hal JAs 7, x. 426 from חלם être fort, solide ; Di Kn compare Talmud חַלְמִית , malva & think of green malachite; Dl HA 36 N derived from Aramaic land A—lamû ), amethyst according to ᵑ9 ᵐ5 Josephus; see also Lag GGA 1884, 285 , but compare Di; one of the gems on the ephod Exod 28:19 ; 39:12 .
